prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1392; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, but I understand you need to identify me. You can use the claim number.
Q: That works. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving on the main road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward the shopping center. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me, so I was stopped at a light.
Q: What happened next?
A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped back and then forward, and my seatbelt locked across my chest. The car behind me hit mine while I was completely stopped.
Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, but I felt dizzy and my neck was really stiff. The other driver came over and apologized. We exchanged insurance information and waited for the police to show up.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: I went to the emergency room later that same day. They took X-rays and told me I had neck and back strain. They gave me a prescription for muscle relaxers and told me to rest.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. My neck still hurts when I turn my head, and my lower back aches after sitting for more than twenty minutes. I've had to take some time off work because of it.
Q: Have you had any prior injuries to your neck or back?
A: I had some minor back soreness a few years ago after lifting boxes, but it went away with stretching. Nothing that required a doctor.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I want to make sure my treatment is covered. I'm following my doctor's instructions and I'm going to physical therapy twice a week.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
